segments.text: Welcome back to GitHub awesome. This is GitHub trending weekly number 41. 35 trending open source projects on GitHub right now. Let's go.
Canvas UI gives your real HTML the kind of WebGL effects normally reserved for a demo reel. Its experimental HTML and
canvas approach lets shaders distort the live DOM so text stays selectable and links remain clickable beneath effects like liquid, glass, and fire. Components
ship as editable source for React, Vue, spelt, or vanilla JavaScript with overlay fallbacks for unsupported browsers.
Openworker is a local first desktop AI co-worker that finishes tasks across your files, terminal, and connected apps
instead of stopping at chat. You can bring an API key from multiple model providers or keep it local with Lama. It
produces documents and reports, supports scheduled runs and approval gates messages, calendar changes, and shell commands.
Thinking orbs gives AI interfaces a loading indicator that says more than still working. It ships six dotted canvas animations for states like
searching, solving, listening, and composing. Each tuned separately for avatar and inline sizes. There's no
WebGL, and the theme follows your app automatically. It also respects reduced motion settings and pauses offscreen.
No AI slop is a writing skill for codecs, claude code, and other agent setups that edits out the habits making machine written pros painfully obvious.
It checks for binary contrasts, empty authority claims, dramatic fragments, inflated importance, and more than 20
other patterns. You can ask it to revise a draft or flag suspicious lines with examples. Then it runs its own pass fail
checks. Basically, it gives your editor an editor.
Sticker Forge turns plain text or uploaded artwork into a WebGL sticker you can grab and peel. The diecut edge
curls under your pointer, revealing a satin back with a shadow projected from the deformed surface. Peel speed also
changes the bundled crackle and tear sounds. It ships as an interactive builder plus a framework independent web
component. So this oddly satisfying interaction can live inside a normal site without rebuilding the renderer.
Bento is a PowerPoint alternative where the presentation and its editor live inside one HTML file. Open it in a
browser, change the deck, then save the same file back with no account or installer. Slides can carry fonts,
images, charts, and animations while the document data stays readable JSON. It even supports encrypted collaboration
through an optional blind relay. That's a refreshingly portable way to own a presentation.
Justify paragraph layout to ordinary web pages, fixing the rivers of whites that browser justification often leaves behind.
Instead of breaking one line at a time, it evaluates the whole paragraph with the new plus algorithm, then adds hyphenation and hanging punctuation
where useful. Unsupported paragraphs simply keep native rendering, which makes this a surprisingly practical typography upgrade.
KO is a native Mac OS terminal workspace built for developers supervising code across multiple repositories.
The terminal stays central while split panes, a file tree, git diffs, and project grouping keep review work nearby
without opening a full IDE. It's written in Swift on top of lib ghosty, and the design favors inspectable actions over
one-click automation. That makes it especially sensible when AI agents are producing changes faster than you should trust them.
Expo Glass Tabs rebuilds the bottom tab bar for Expo Router with native liquid glass materials and more useful minimize
behavior. Scroll down and the pill shrinks while every icon remains visible. Drag across it and the highlight follows your finger with
haptic ticks before navigating on release.
Animation stays on the UI thread while older iOS versions in Android get a solid fall back.
PIL Studio is a browser-based video editor built specifically for talking head clips with no account or backend required for the core workflow. Drop in
footage, then shape it with a timeline, kinetic captions, designed graphics, and reusable visual themes. Drafts and video
bytes stay in browser storage while Chromium handles export through webc.
You can also drive the editor from codeex or another agent over MCP.
RWX turns Unix file permissions from a memorized chmod puzzle into an interactive terminal interace. Browse to
a file, toggle read, write, and execute bits in a grid, or enter octal directly and watch the symbolic mode update in real time. It also handles owners,
groups, special bits, and recursive changes with validation before applying them.
The last language model anyone squeezed onto a chip like this held 260,000 parameters because everything has to fit
in half a megabyte of fast memory. This one leaves the 25 million row embedding table sitting in flash and pulls roughly
450 bytes per token. So only the thinking core needs a trained on tiny stories. So it writes short stories and nothing else on an $8 ESP32.
When your agent hands work to a sub agent that runs long, the main conversation's prompt cache quietly expires and the next turn re-encodes the whole history at the full right rate.
Claude Thermos sits in front as a local proxy, watches for that idle window, and replays the last request capped at a
single token to refresh the prefix. Each session logs what warming cost and what it avoided.
Token tab turns the session logs your coding agents already leave behind into a local usage statement. It reads codecs
claude code then breaks tokens and estimated cost down by model project day and activity. The CLI can emit JSON
while a local host dashboard adds charts without uploading anything. Pricing is a handmaintained table and activity labels are heruristic.
Neat annotations adds handdrawn arrows, labels, and marker highlights to inline web content using one CSS file. Wrap a
target in a span, choose one of eight directions, and put the note in a data attribute. There's no JavaScript or build step. Colors are controlled with
classes or variables, and animated effects respect reduced motion settings.
Agent execution partnership is a control plane that sits between an AI agent's decision and the action it wants to run.
Each proposal gets checked against identity, capability, policy and risk, then executes as one bounded action with
postrun verification. Consequential operations can require human approval and every stage lands in an appendon audit trail.
MinSQLite is a Rust reimplementation of SQLite that stays compatible with the official database file format. So it can
open files written by SQLite 3 and write them back. The public API is just one connection type with four methods while underneath it implements queries,
transactions, wall, crash recovery, and the storage engine itself. The maintainers report 5,650 tests and no unsafe library code.
Live tennis API MCP gives Claude, Cursor, and other MCP clients direct access to current tennis data instead of
making the model guess. Its readonly tools cover live scores, fixtures, player searches, and recent results across ATP, WTA, challenger, and ITF
events. It also understands subscription tiers, so a blocked endpoint returns the required plan instead of a vague failure.
Jelly UI is a web components library where buttons, toggles, and inputs physically wobble when you interact with them. The fun part doesn't replace the
boring essentials. Controls use native focus, keyboard behavior, standard events, and form data with reduced
motion support built in. It has zero runtime dependencies, and ships as one ESM bundle.
Running a 26 billion parameter model normally means owning the RAM to hold all 14 GB of it. Turbo Fieldfare keeps
only the shared core and KV cache resident around two and streams each token's experts off the SSD as the
router picks them. Custom Swift and Metal kernels the whole way down. No MLX or Llama CPP underneath. The author
measured roughly five tokens a second on an 8 GB M2 Air.
Draw Your Font turns a photo of your handwriting into an installable type face entirely on your own machine. Its node CLI detects each letter, vectorizes
the shapes, and exports TTF, WAFT, WAFT 2, and CSS. You can use a printable template for cleaner results, or hand
claude code a messy notebook photo and refine letters conversationally. Kerning and liatures aren't here yet, so the output is a single variant font, not a full type family.
Agent council is a skill that asks several installed AI command line tools the same question, then has a configurable chairman combine their
answers. Codeex, Claude Code, and other CLIs respond independently and in parallel, so you can compare reasoning
instead of trusting the first output. It uses your existing CLI subscriptions rather than separate API calls. Useful for tricky decisions, although the
slowest member still sets the response time.
Mac OS Laguna S2.1 is a reproducible benchmark harness for comparing local quantizations of poolside's coding model
on Apple silicon. It records raw outputs, task scores, throughput, memory, revisions, and machine details,
so speed claims keep their context. On a 128 GB M5 Max, the project reports a two-bit build passing all 38 assertions while averaging 63.86 tokens per second.
Every Frontier release restarts the same argument about which model to switch to.
Fusion harness runs two instead. One plans, one builds, and a third pass merges both answers with attribution for
what each contributed. The autov validate loop is the sharper part. A validator writes the acceptance test before any code exists, and that test
has to fail on the first run or the harness warns you the gate is too weak to trust.
Optical modeler is an agent skill that turns 2D phatonic schematics into auditable Blender optical tables with geometry treated as evidence instead of
decoration. It checks real apertures, beam continuity, table holes, fasteners, supports, and fiber bends, then reopens the saved scene for mesh and ray tests.
The output includes renders, reports, manifests, and hashes.
Rebuilding a volcano plot or a circus diagram from a paper usually starts with hunting for the author's data which is
not published either. This repo skips that 20 journal figure types each with a simulator that generates its own data
from a fixed seed and a plot script beside it. Nothing to download and swapping in your real numbers means
matching the column names. A runner renders all 20 and prints which ones broke.
PG context turns Postgress SQL 17 or 18 into a hybrid search engine. So vectors, metadata, permissions, and backups stay
beside your application data instead of moving to another service. It combines HNSU vector search with Postgress full text ranking, supports filter
approximate search, and rechecks every candidate against live rows and rowle security. The team reports 3.8 to 5.3
times faster queries than PG vector in one benchmark.
A wall tablet running Home Assistant in a browser can't hear you once the screen goes dark. And on a plain HTTP instance,
the browser refuses the microphone entirely. Kiosk Satellite runs the wakeword natively instead, listening with the screen off or another app in
front and routes the dashboard through a loop back proxy, so an HTTP instance counts as a secure context. Remote admin runs from any browser on your network.
Most agent frameworks assume you're paying prices, so their tool layer burns calls the cheap models can't afford.
Penguin Harness trims the tool set down and tunes it for open models like DeepS, then lets an agent scaffold a whole
agent app from one sentence. It runs its own benchmark, finds where it lost points, and ships the next version with
a snapshot taken first. Collage B-roll explainers is a clawed code skill that turns one spoken sentence into a
5-second vertical paper collage animation. It proposes visual metaphors first, waits for approval, generates a
still, then animates the pieces assembling from an empty frame. Local FFmpeg steps verify the opening, compare the final frame, and fit an optional voice over.
Fin loop is a three-skll workflow that turns linear and GitHub into a small clawed code software factory without
letting agents merge their own work. One skill interviews you and writes the spec. Another claims approved issues and
opens pull requests and a third reviews each PR against its acceptance criteria and required checks. Humans apply the ready label and perform the final merge.
Compliance work usually lives in a spreadsheet nobody trusts and a shared drive nobody can navigate. Conformity
gives all 217 controls across SOCK 2, ISO 2701 and PCIDSS an actual folder tree on disk with RO
and folder permissions that cascade down it. Documents carry a review cadence and a daily scan emails the owner as each
deadline approaches. Every create and delete lands in a readonly audit log.
Block diffusion models decode one block at a time and every block waits for the one before it to finalize. FlowBlock
treats that finality as optional. A downstream block can start from a good draft since these models correct tokens
later anyway. A gate decides when a block is ready to spawn. Commits stay in order and each request gets its own
wavefront so batched serving stays dense.
Boss Console is a cross-platform operator workspace that lets codecs, claude code share the same browser, terminal, editor, and MCP tool set.
Every tool can be allowed or disabled.
Secrets can fill browser forms without entering model context, and plugins hot reload while the app keeps running. It's JVM based rather than Electron, and even
lets you share an encrypted terminal session to a phone.
SimSlim lets one Mac run far more iOS simulators by disabling background services that development and CI usually
don't need. The maintainers measured memory dropping from 4 GB to 0.9 per simulator on their M1 Pro test. Profiles
let you preserve features like push notifications or store kit. And a doctor command catches broken requirements before tests start.
